item.title: Lecture 1
item.description: Definition DG1.1(Definition). i) A differentiable curve (C^\infty) is a map \alpha: I \mapsto \mathbb{R^3} where I=(a,b)\subset \mathbb{R} such that \alpha \in C^\infty(I).

item.title: Lecture 2
item.description: Remark DG2.1(Remark). Recall that we have \alpha:I\mapsto \mathbb{R}^3 with t_0\in I depicted by: Definition DG2.2(Definition). Let s:I\mapsto\mathbb{R} be defined by s(t)=\int^t_{t_0}|\alpha'(u)|du = L^t_{t_0}(\alpha).

item.title: Lecture 3
item.description: As usual, consider \alpha:I\mapsto \mathbb{R}^3 p.a.l. with k>0, s\mapsto\begin{pmatrix}T(s)\\ N(s)\\ B(s)\end{pmatrix}\in \mathbb{R}^3. Then, \begin{pmatrix}T'(s)\\ N'(s)\\ B'(s)\end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix}k(s)N(S)\\ -k(s)T(s)-\tau(s)B(s)\\ \tau(s)N(s)\end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix}O_3 & k(s)\mathrm{I}_3 & O_3\\ -k(s)\mathrm{I}_3 & O_3 & -\tau(s)\mathrm{I}_3\\ O_3 & \tau(s)\mathrm{I}_3 & O_3\end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix}T(s)\\ N(s)\\ B(s)\end{pmatrix} Theorem DG3.1(Fundamental theorem of the local theory of curves).

item.title: Lecture 4
item.description: Definition DG4.1(Definition). A subset S of \mathbb{R}^3 is a regular surface if \forall p \in S, \exists an open set V\subset\mathbb{R}^3 such that p\in V and \exists \overline{X}:U\mapsto V where U is an open set of \mathbb{R}^2, \overline{X} is surjective and \overline{X} is a C^\infty map.
